source: Bezakova, Galanis, Goldberg, Guo, Stefankovic, SICOMP 2019 (arXiv:1510.09193); Moitra JACM 2019; Galanis-Guo-Wang
statement: Approximate #SAT of (k,Delta)-CNF: FPTAS for Delta <= c*2^(k/2)/k (Moitra); NP-hard (NP=RP) for Delta >= c*2^(k/2). Threshold exponent k/2.

conclusion: For F0 unsatisfiable with j=min{i:a_i>0} and F_t = F0 AND (t disjoint satisfiable 3-clauses on fresh vars), the shifted polynomial P(lambda)=Z_F(lambda)+c (c>0) has j zeros within 2(c/(A0 7^t))^(1/j)=2^-Omega(t) of [0,1] (Rouche on |lambda|=R_t). So no class containing an UNSAT formula and closed under fresh-clause padding has a uniform-width zero-free neighbourhood of [0,1] for P.
justification: Z multiplicative over variable-disjoint conjunction; Rouche comparison c+A lambda^j h vs c+A lambda^j; exact finite check on F0=all 8 clauses on 3 vars matches 1/(16 7^t)

approach: O2: decide SAT beyond the always-satisfiable region via an instance-dependent zero-free (Lee-Yang/Barvinok) criterion on Z_F
reopen_if: a polynomial/weighting whose zero-free region provably extends past variable-degree 2^(k/2) on a SAT-hard class (which by BGGGS would imply NP=RP), OR a non-Barvinok interpolation usable at zero-free width o(1/log n)
why: Zero-free interpolation computes #SAT only on the counting-tractable region (degree <~ 2^(k/2)/k), which is exponentially below f(k)~2^k/k (SAT trivial, all-YES) and a factor ~k below the counting-hardness threshold 2^(k/2). It cannot reach the NP-hard decision regime. On padded classes the forced zero cannot be shifted away (Z2, PROVEN). Earlier ETH argument (Z3) superseded by this degree-threshold placement.

source: Liu, Wang, Yin, Zhang, Zhou, arXiv:2608.08616v3 (Oct 2026), A Counting and Sampling Lovasz Local Lemma
statement: Approximate counting and sampling of CSP solutions are tractable in the regime 4e*p*(D+1)^2 <= 1 (p=max violation prob, D=max dependency degree); tight up to constants under NP!=RP. For k-SAT: D <~ 2^(k/2). Deterministic approx counting, randomized approx counting, near-linear EXACT SAMPLING (not exact counting).

summary: Exact: F0=all 8 clauses on 3 vars gives Z_F0=8*lambda; Z_{F_t}=8*lambda*(7+lambda)^t. Zeros of the partition polynomial itself: lambda=0 (=#SAT) and lambda=-7 only; padding adds zeros only at -7. The exp-small distance of Z2 appears ONLY for Z+c with fixed c (d: 6.25e-2,1.28e-3,2.60e-5 for t=0,2,4); dividing by 7^t restores constant distance ~0.064. => normalization artifact.

evidence: Normalization test cm-673ff95932cb4a11: zeros of Z itself under padding lie only at 0 (=#SAT) and -7; the near-[0,1] zero is produced solely by adding a FIXED constant c to a polynomial whose coefficients grow like 7^t, and vanishes under division by 7^t or 2^n. The Rouche computation is correct; its reading as an intrinsic/universal obstruction is withdrawn.
statement: The SOSA-independent claim 'zero-free interpolation faces an intrinsic padding obstruction: no class closed under fresh-clause padding has a uniform-width zero-free neighbourhood of [0,1] for P=Z_F+c' (T6 Z2 conclusion).

approach: O2 (revised): decide SAT above f(k) via an efficiently constructible instance-dependent zero-free / algebraic certificate

Honest status: counting/zero-free methods are confined to the pD^2 regime (D <~ 2^(k/2), tight under NP!=RP, 2608.08616), which lies strictly inside the all-YES decision region (pD regime, D <~ 2^k); so they say nothing new about decision hardness, and a poly certificate deciding SAT above f(k) would itself be P=NP (no free lunch, as O0/PCZT). O2 is de-prioritized as a face of the open problem, NOT closed by a barrier.

statement: A bipartite graph is Pfaffian (has a Pfaffian orientation; FKT computes #perfect-matchings via a Pfaffian) iff it is built by 4-sums from planar bipartite braces and one sporadic nonplanar brace (the Heawood graph); poly-time recognizable. K_{3,3} is the minimal non-Pfaffian bipartite graph.

source: Mignon-Ressayre 2004; Cai-Chen-Li; Yabe
statement: Determinantal complexity dc(perm_n) >= n^2/2 (char 0, Hessian-rank method), >= (n-1)^2+1 over R; extends to char != 2. All proven bounds quadratic; superpolynomial dc(perm) = VP_ws != VNP, open.

summary: Exhaustive 2^9 search: K_{3,3} has NO Pfaffian orientation (no edge-signing makes all 6 perfect matchings agree in sign); K_{2,2} does. K_{2,2} signing (+,+,+,-): Pf=ad+bc=perm, det=(ad+bc)^2=perm^2 (symbolic, sympy).

conclusion: Lemma O1-B: if a poly-time algorithm maps every bipartite G to a skew-symmetric integer matrix B(G) with Pf(B(G))=#PM(G), then FP=#P (so P=P^#P, PH collapses).
justification: Pfaffian of an integer skew matrix is exactly poly-time (Mahajan-Subramanya-Vinay fraction-free, value+sign); compose with the poly-time construction to get #PM in FP; #PM bipartite = 0/1-permanent = #P-complete (Valiant). Reviewed VALID.

conclusion: Lemma O1-A: Pf(M)=perm_n for affine skew M of size 2m implies det(M)=perm_n^2, so pf-dc(perm_n) >= (1/2) dc(perm_n^2); dc and pf-dc are polynomially equivalent (determinant and Pfaffian both VP_ws-complete).
justification: Pf^2=det; both complete for VP_ws. Base case K_{2,2} verified symbolically (cm-d55440f1d9d84caf). Reviewed VALID.

statement: pf-dc(perm_n) = Omega(n^2) (affine Pfaffian complexity of the permanent is at least quadratic).

why: Four models separated. Local (L) fails off planar+Heawood (RST; K_{3,3} counterexample). Instance-dependent poly-constructible (I) = FP=#P exactly (O1-B, no free lunch). The only lever with upside is the symbolic affine model (S): dc/pf-dc(perm), where proven bounds are quadratic and superpolynomial = VP_ws != VNP (necessary for VP != VNP, which does NOT directly give P != NP). source: OpenAI (24 Sep 2026), cubic border determinantal complexity; Sheshadri arXiv:2610.40484 (29 Oct 2026) Thm 1.1/1.2/3.1
statement: A smooth degree-d hypersurface in N variables has border dc >= (N-1)(d-1)/(4e) and pc >= (N-1)(d-1)/(8e). Consequences: dc_bar(perm_n)=Omega(n^3) (border, char 0, OpenAI); pc(perm_n)=Omega(n^3) and dc over every odd characteristic (Sheshadri); degree-a entries give dc_a,pc_a(perm_n)=Omega(n^3/a). Proof: intersect V(F) with N-2 general first derivatives, multiplicities sum d(d-1)^{N-2}, carried through the border limit.

source: Pant, Singh, arXiv:2605.21077 (2026)

CORRECTION of the earlier PNP-001 claim that quadratic determinantal bounds (Mignon-Ressayre n^2/2) are the frontier: superseded by the 2026 cubic bounds above. My earlier O1-A conjecture pf-dc(perm_n)=Omega(n^2) (recorded HYPOTHESIS) is RESOLVED and strengthened to pc(perm_n)=Omega(n^3) by Sheshadri Thm 1.1. The perm^2 route I had proposed is unnecessary and was in any case blocked ({perm^2=0} non-reduced). The frontier is cubic; the gap to superpolynomial (= VP_ws != VNP, hence necessary-but-not-sufficient for VP != VNP, which does NOT give P != NP) remains wide open.

conclusion: Proposition O1-E: the smooth-restriction/polar-intersection method (Sheshadri Thm 3.1 / OpenAI) applied to perm_n via affine restrictions cannot prove any lower bound exceeding (n^2-1)(n-1)/(4e) < n^3/(4e) (resp. n^3/(8e) for Pfaffians), because an affine restriction F' of perm_n has degree <= n and, by smoothness (else the zero locus is a cone), <= n^2 variables, and dc(F') <= dc(perm_n).
justification: dc(F')<=dc(perm_n) by pullback of a determinantal rep under the affine map; degree non-increasing under affine substitution; N'<=n^2 forced by smoothness. Independently verified VALID by adversarial reviewer (strong model) with the cone/singularity sharpening of N'<=n^2.

conclusion: Lemma O1-C: pc(F) <= 2 dc(F) via B=[[0,A],[-A^T,0]] (alternating order 2m, Pf B = (-1)^{m(m-1)/2} det A, sign fixed to + by a transposition); and det(M)=Pf(M)^2 gives dc(F^2) <= pc(F). A LINEAR reverse dc(F) <= C*pc(F) is NOT known (only polynomial via VP_ws-completeness); the det->Pf (easy) vs Pf->det (needs a square root, not linear) asymmetry is genuine.
justification: Block-embedding identity with exact sign; VP_ws polynomial equivalence. Verified VALID by adversarial reviewer, who supplied the exact raw sign (-1)^{m(m-1)/2} and the transposition fix.

question: Does a LINEAR reverse bound dc(F) <= C*pc(F) hold for an absolute constant C, or only the polynomial relation (both VP_ws-complete)?
why: Settles whether determinantal and Pfaffian affine models are the same up to constants or genuinely differ; the 2026 cubic bounds (dc>=.../(4e), pc>=.../(8e)) are consistent with pc~dc/2 but do not establish it.

source: standard (Jacobian criterion; Pfaffian adjugate); owner-sharpened 2026-11-17; verified by adversarial review
statement: Singular criterion for affine Pfaffian reps F(x)=Pf(A_0+sum x_i A_i): x in Sing(V(F)) iff F(x)=0 AND DF_x=0, iff corank A(x)>=4 OR (corank A(x)=2 and u^T A_i v=0 for all i), where u,v span ker A(x). At corank 2, D(Pf)_M(H)=c_M u^T H v with c_M=Pf(A')!=0 (adjugate ~ uv^T-vu^T). Intrinsic locus (corank>=4) codim 6; tangency condition codim 1.

summary: Counterexample A(x,y)=[[0,1,x,0],[-1,0,0,-y],[-x,0,0,0],[0,y,0,0]]: Pf(A)=xy exactly; A(0,0) corank 2 (kernel e3,e4); grad Pf dual to (3,4)-entry; (A_1)_{34}=(A_2)_{34}=0 so im(L) in tangent hyperplane. Origin is tangency-induced (corank 2), NOT intrinsic (corank 4).

conclusion: Lemma T8-B: at a tangency-induced singular point p of F=Pf(A(x)) (A(p) corank 2, kernel u,v, u^T A_i v=0 for all i), rank Hess_F(p) <= 4m-4.
justification: Pfaffian Schur-complement Pf([[X,Y],[-Y^T,Z]])=Pf(Z)Pf(X + Y Z^-1 Y^T) (sign + verified exactly); tangency makes (H11)_12=u^T H v identically 0, so F is quadratic-leading through the 2x(2m-2) block H12; Hessian factors through H12, dim 4m-4. Elementary corollary of the classical Schur identity, NOT a deep theorem. Verified: PI derivation + gpt-oss-120b (independent, gave sign minus) + exact sympy (rank=8=4m-4 tight, 40 random instances by the reviewer never exceed 4m-4) + adversarial review VALID WITH FIXES (sign +, downgrade 'original').

approach: O1: use tangency / Pfaffian singular-locus geometry to get a lower bound on affine Pfaffian complexity pc(perm_n) beyond cubic
reopen_if: a proof that a singular point of perm_n with Hessian rank Theta(n^2) is forced to be corank-2 (tangency) in every affine Pfaffian representation (would give pc=Omega(n^2)); or a global Pfaffian method replacing the local Hessian
why: Local tangency-Hessian method is capped by rank Hess <= 4m-4 per point (Lemma T8-B), giving at most pc(perm_n)>=(R+4)/2 with R the Hessian rank at a tangency-realizable SINGULAR point of perm. It is local/single-point and CANNOT reach Sheshadri's global cubic bound. Whether it gives quadratic or only linear depends on the open R; the gpt-oss claim R=2n is unverified and NOT adopted (conflicts with MR ~n^2). The crux is the singular-point (grad perm=0) vs mere-zero (perm=0) distinction - MR's rank-n^2 point is a zero, not necessarily a singular point realizable as corank-2.

question: What is the maximal rank of Hess(perm_n) at a SINGULAR point of perm_n (perm=0 AND grad perm=0) that is realizable as a corank-2 (tangency) point of an affine Pfaffian representation - Theta(n^2) (giving pc=Omega(n^2) via Lemma T8-B) or only O(n)? And can a representation force all high-Hessian-rank singular points into the codim-6 corank-4 locus?
why: Determines whether tangency geometry yields a quadratic Pfaffian lower bound or is stuck at linear; it is the exact next proof obligation for the directive's simultaneous-tangency problem.

statement: pc(perm_4) in [8,30], exact value OPEN: lower bound 8 (Pf of order 2m has degree m, perm_4 degree 4 => m>=4 => pc=2m>=8); upper bound 30 (pc<=2 dc, Grenet dc(perm_4)<=2^4-1=15; the Nov 2026 exact dc(perm_4)=15 is a tighter reference but gives the same <=30). dc(perm_4)=15 does NOT determine pc(perm_4).

conclusion: Corank-stratified Hessian bounds for affine Pfaffian reps F=Pf(A(x)) at a singular point p: corank 2 => rank Hess_F(p) <= 4m-4 (T8-B); corank 4 => rank <= 6; corank >=6 => rank = 0. Corollary: rank Hess_F(p) > 6 ==> corank A(p)=2.
justification: corank-4: split off invertible skew block, residual 4x4 kernel-Pfaffian quadratic in its 6 entries; corank>=6: kernel-Pfaffian expansion starts at order>=3. Verified exactly (sympy, m=4): corank-4 rank=6 (tight), corank-6 rank=0; corank-2 rank=8=4m-4 (m=3). Independent review of the corank-2 case VALID (T8-B); corank-4/6 derivations under review.

summary: Max Hessian rank on Sing(V(perm_n)) grows at least QUADRATICALLY. Owner construction X=diag(B,C), perm(B)=perm(C)=0 with full-rank gradients, k+l=n, k,l>=2 => rank Hess(perm_n)(X)=2kl+2; with k=floor(n/2),l=ceil(n/2): M_n >= floor(n^2/2)+2. Search n=4: 167408 matrices over {-1,0,1}, 873 singular, MAX rank=10 = block construction (optimal at n=4, tested not proven). So M_n=Theta(n^2).

conclusion: pc(perm_n)=2m >= (M_n+4)/2 UNCONDITIONALLY (m>=(M_n+4)/4), where M_n=max Hessian rank over Sing(V(perm_n)); since M_n >= floor(n^2/2)+2 (quadratic), pc(perm_n)=Omega(n^2) from local singular-locus geometry.
justification: The corollary removes the realizability caveat: any singular point with Hessian rank>6 is corank-2, so T8-B applies and 4m-4 >= rank. Owner construction gives a rank>6 witness for every n>=4. Quadratic, below Sheshadri's cubic pc=Omega(n^3). Novelty NOT claimed (the 2kl+2 formula may be in the literature; singular-locus geometry of perm is open, 2024).

conclusion: Corank-4 bound PROVEN (normal form, not finite search): at a singular point p of F=Pf(A(x)) with corank A(p)=4, rank Hess_F(p) <= 6. Corank>=6 bound PROVEN: rank Hess_F(p)=0.
justification: Pfaffian Schur complement F=Pf(A'+H22)Pf(H11 + H12(A'+H22)^-1 H12^T). Corank 4: DPf=0 (no linear term); Pf of 4x4 is the homogeneous quadratic af-be+cd, so the degree-2 part of F is Pf(A')Pf(H11), factoring through the 6 entries of the 4x4 kernel block H11 => rank<=6. Corank>=6: Pf of 2r x 2r (r>=3) is homogeneous of degree r>=3, so F starts at order>=3 => Hessian=0. Elementary via the local Pfaffian normal form. Numerically consistent (rank 6 tight, 0) but the PROOF is the normal form, not the finite check.

conclusion: Corollary (THEOREM, from the proven corank-stratified bounds): for an affine Pfaffian representation F=Pf(A(x)), rank Hess_F(p) > 6 implies corank A(p) = 2.
justification: A singular point with Hessian rank >6 cannot be corank 4 (<=6) or >=6 (=0), so it is corank 2. Now proven (not just tested), so the unconditional bound pc=2m >= (rank+4)/2 for any such point is rigorous.

conclusion: Tangent-space bound (Fall D tool): for any singular point X of perm_n, rank Hess(perm_n)(X) <= n^2 - dim_X Sigma, where Sigma=Sing(V(perm_n))={grad perm_n=0}. In particular the torus orbit (dim <= 2n-1) gives rank <= n^2-(2n-1), recovering the connected torus bound.
justification: Hess(perm_n) is the Jacobian of the map grad(perm_n): C^{n^2}->C^{n^2}; Sigma = {grad perm_n = 0} is its zero locus, so the Zariski tangent space T_X Sigma = ker Hess, giving dim ker Hess >= dim_X Sigma, i.e. rank Hess <= n^2 - dim_X Sigma. Consequence: M_5=14 would follow if every connected singular point lies in a component of Sigma(perm_5) of dimension >= 11. Whether dim Sigma(perm_5) >= 11 on connected components is OPEN (singular-locus geometry of perm, 2024 literature).

statement: For char != 2, dim K[X]/I_h(a,b) = max(a,b)(h-1) for 1<=h<=min(a,b), h<max(a,b). Consequently codim Crit(perm_n) = 2n, i.e. dim Sigma(perm_n) = n(n-2); for n=5, dim Sigma(perm_5)=15. The dimension is realized by the family supported on h-1=n-2 rows (the '2-zero-rows' family for n=5, which has Hessian rank 2n=10). Xie explicitly states the dimension calc does NOT imply reducedness; the complete-intersection/reduced result (Thm 1.3) is ONLY for maximal permanents I_k(k,k+1), NOT for the square critical locus I_{n-1}(n,n). No equidimensionality or minimal-component-dimension statement.

REFRAMING of M_5 via Xie + the tangent-space bound. rank Hess(perm_5)(X) = 25 - dim T_X Sigma (Zariski tangent space to Crit(perm_5)=V(I_4(5,5))), <= 25 - dim_X Sigma (LOCAL dim). Our data give TWO components: (i) the n-2=3-row-supported '2-zero-rows' family, dim = n(n-2)=15 (Xie's maximal component), Hessian rank 10; (ii) the block family diag(B,C), dim 11, Hessian rank 14. So Sigma(perm_5) is NOT equidimensional. M_5 = 25 - d_min where d_min = minimal tangent-space dim over singular points. Xie gives the MAXIMAL dim (15) -> rank 10 there, which does NOT bound M_5 from above. M_5=14 IFF no component of Sigma(perm_5) has dim <= 10 (at a point with reduced/<=10-dim tangent space). Xie does NOT settle this (gives max, not min, dim; reducedness of I_4(5,5) open).

statement: They DO describe the irreducible components of the RECTANGULAR permanental variety P_{k,k+1} = {all k x k permanents of a generic k x (k+1) matrix vanish}. Prop 4.12: ALL irreducible components of P_{4,5} (a 4x5 matrix, 20 variables) have codimension 5 - i.e. P_{4,5} IS equidimensional (dim 15). Components: linear spaces from a vanishing row (Prop 3.8, L_k) and 'other types from vanishing linear forms in a column' (Rem 3.9), all codim k+1. Table 1 lists the components of P_{4,5}.

PRIOR-ART CORRECTION (protect against claiming known results as new). CRUCIAL distinction: Boralevi et al. 2025's equidimensionality result is for the RECTANGULAR variety P_{4,5} (4x5 matrix, 20 vars, all 4x4 permanents=0). Our non-equidimensionality result is for the SQUARE critical locus Sigma(perm_5)=Crit(perm_5) (5x5 matrix, 25 vars, all 4x4 sub-permanents=0) - a DIFFERENT variety (different ambient dim 25 vs 20, different equations 25 vs 5). Our block component V_{2,3}=diag(B_{2x2},C_{3x3}) is square-specific and not in their rectangular Table 1. KNOWN components reused: the 15-dim vanishing-row linear spaces (Boralevi Prop 3.8; Xie) and the W_{1,4} vanishing-row+col+complementary-perm type (Blaeser et al 2017). STATUS OF NOVELTY: the SQUARE non-equidimensionality and the explicit 11-dim block component V_{2,3} were NOT found in the surveyed literature (Boralevi 2025 is rectangular-equidimensional; Xie 2026 global-dim-only; Blaeser 2017 / Kirkup 2005 do not address it), but a FULL novelty determination requires confirming no prior treatment of the SQUARE critical locus's component/equidimensionality structure. We do NOT claim the result as definitively new; the VERIFIED FACT (Sigma(perm_5) non-equidimensional, dim 11 and 15, three-way exact) stands regardless of novelty.

Deeper read of Boralevi-Carlini-Michalek-Ventura (Adv.Math.2025) sec 4.5: the partition/torus geometry is ALREADY established there (Prop 4.2, Cor 4.17; Def 4.24, Lemma 4.25: I(Sigma(perm_n)) subset J_{R1}+J_{R2} for a row partition; Cor 4.26: such a component has codim >= k+1 (not =), so a codim-14/dim-11 component is explicitly allowed; Conjecture 4.27). VERIFIED EXACTLY: our V_{2,3}=diag(B,C) lies in the partition variety V(J_{S1}+J_{S2}) for the row partition S1={0,1},S2={2,3,4} (all 10 two-perms of rows{0,1}=0 and all 10 three-perms of rows{2,3,4}=0 at X_A). So V_{2,3} is one of the partition subvarieties PREDICTED by Conjecture 4.27 - it does NOT lie outside them and does NOT refute Conj 4.27.

Separation of verified fact vs novelty for T9. VERIFIED FACTS (four-way exact, keep): (1) Sigma(perm_5) has a genuine smooth 11-dim component V_{2,3} through X_A (dim T_{X_A}Sigma=11 forces the component through X_A to be dim 11; the 15-dim pieces of the enclosing partition variety carry a zero row, which X_A lacks); (2) Sigma(perm_5) is NOT equidimensional (dim 11 and 15 components). NOT ESTABLISHED: that this is the FIRST proof of non-equidimensionality (prior art unresolved); that it refutes Conjecture 4.27 (it does not - V_{2,3} is in a predicted partition variety). A genuine attack on Conj 4.27 would need a singular point lying in NO partition variety; we do NOT have one. Dimension note (corrected): the partition product variety has global dim dim P_{2,5}+dim P_{3,5}=5+10=15 (Xie Thm), but that does not exclude its own dim-11 sub-component V_{2,3} (Thm 3.18/1.1 claim no equidimensionality).

T9 CLOSED. Precise delineation vs Boralevi et al. 2025 sec 4.5 (point-by-point). KNOWN (prior art): the partition/torus framework and the CONTAINMENT V_{2,3} subset V(J_{S1}+J_{S2}) (Def 4.24, Lemma 4.25: partition varieties are in Sing(perm)); Cor 4.26 gives codim >= 2k (not =), so a dim-11 piece is allowed; Conjecture 4.27 posits Sing = union of partition varieties. NOT implied by sec 4.5 (our standalone contribution): that V_{2,3} is an irreducible COMPONENT of Sigma(perm_5) and that Sigma(perm_5) is non-equidimensional. Reason: even assuming Conj 4.27, set-theoretic containment does NOT show V_{2,3} is a component - it could be covered by a higher-dim (15) component of another partition variety (e.g. a (1,4) partition or a zero-row piece). Our EXACT tangent-space computation dim T_{X_A}Sigma = 25 - rank H(X_A) = 25-14 = 11 gives the UNCONDITIONAL component proof (no component covers V_{2,3} at X_A) and the UNCONDITIONAL non-equidimensionality - a question Boralevi (equidim open for the SQUARE Sing) and Xie (global dim only) leave open. NOVELTY STATUS: PRIOR_ART_UNRESOLVED (containment known; the component/non-equidim proof via Hessian rank not found in surveyed literature, full determination still open). No refutation of Conjecture 4.27 is claimed (V_{2,3} lies in a predicted partition variety).

statement: T10-A: There exists a constant M such that for all m > M and every n > 2m^2+2m, any tau, and any k<n, rank((l^{n-m} perm_m)_{(k,n-k)[tau]}) < rank((det_n)_{(k,n-k)[tau]}). So the shifted-partial-derivatives measure of the PADDED permanent never exceeds that of det_n above the quadratic threshold => SPD cannot prove dc(perm_m)=omega(m^2) in this model. SCOPE: holds for sufficiently large m (NOT all m); the paper EXPLICITLY leaves open general Young flattenings / minimal free resolutions (may reach omega(m^2)).

Does failure of the sum identity for |v \ u| ≥ 2 allow ratio > k at all? The decisive test is whether a multi-difference matrix on the 41-row domain can have every clause-restricted rank ≤ 1 while total rank ≥ 21. This is the sub-case that D-014 leaves open. Without a result there, neither the single-difference limitation nor the dense control says anything about whether D-013 can be improved.

conclusion: If every nonzero entry A[u,v] of a Gal matrix has |v \ u| = 1, the Gal ratio is at most k = C(n,3): each such entry lies in exactly one clause rectangle R_j, so A = sum_j A|R_j with disjoint supports and rank(A) <= sum_j rank(A|R_j) <= k * max_j rank(A|R_j). Any improvement over k must use entries with |v \ u| >= 2.
